transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

My mind just won’t slow down—ideas are racing all the time and I can’t keep my thoughts straight anymore. It's just gotten to the point where I feel completely overwhelmed trying to keep up with everything.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy, or have you mostly felt anxious and unable to relax?

Yes, I've only been sleeping about three or four hours a night, but I wake up feeling completely wired and full of energy instead of tired. I'll lie in bed planning resident programs or art projects, and then I just have to get up and start cleaning, reorganizing, or working on new tasks. It's definitely a buzzing energy rather than just feeling anxious.
Have these symptoms caused any serious problems at work, with money, relationships, or led to risky behavior, or are you still able to function fairly normally?

Yes, it's caused a lot of trouble. My supervisor cut my hours and put me under closer supervision because my charting got so unreliable, and I've fallen behind in my evening class. I've also pulled away from my family and friends, spending most of my free time alone on the couch instead of doing my hobbies.
Have you had any hallucinations, delusional beliefs, or become so disorganized that other people had trouble understanding you?

Yes, I've been hearing a man's voice whispering my name and commenting on what I'm doing when I'm alone, and I'm convinced my coworkers and teacher are secretly changing schedules to sabotage my promotion. I also get so confused that I'll pace around talking to myself, or sometimes I just freeze up entirely in the break room and can't speak.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with a manic episode with psychotic symptoms: elevated/expansive energized state, racing thoughts, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, marked functional impairment, and clear mood-congruent/incongruent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions). The severity and psychosis support F30.2 over hypomania or bipolar disorder not otherwise specified from the limited history.
